content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To try fishing for the first time, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase a regional fishing guidebook (30 minutes)
Step 2. Research local fish species habitats (1 hour)
Step 3. Buy a sturdy tackle box (20 minutes)
Step 4. Watch online tutorials on rod assembly (45 minutes)
Step 5. Check the weather forecast for the weekend (5 minutes)
Step 6. Apply for a basic fishing license online (15 minutes)
Step 7. Practice casting in an open field (1 hour)
Step 8. Visit a local bait shop for advice (30 minutes)
Step 9. Purchase a spool of monofilament line (10 minutes)
Step 10. Buy a set of assorted sinkers (10 minutes)
Step 11. Select a variety of artificial lures (25 minutes)
Step 12. Organize all gear into the tackle box (40 minutes)
Step 13. Learn how to tie a Clinch knot (15 minutes)
Step 14. Download a GPS map of the lake (10 minutes)
Step 15. Buy a comfortable folding chair (20 minutes)
Step 16. Assemble the two-piece fishing rod (5 minutes)
Step 17. Attach the reel to the rod seat (10 minutes)
Step 18. Pack a cooler with drinks and ice (15 minutes)
Step 19. Look up boat rental prices (10 minutes)
Step 20. Read a "Fishing for Beginners" blog post (20 minutes)
Step 21. Apply sunscreen and bug spray (5 minutes)
Step 22. Set up the fishing spot on the pier (15 minutes)
Step 23. Thread the line through the rod guides (10 minutes)
Step 24. Buy a pair of polarized sunglasses (30 minutes)
Step 25. Place a first-aid kit in the tackle box (5 minutes)
Step 26. Pack a pair of needle-nose pliers (5 minutes)
Step 27. Drive to the designated fishing location (1 hour)
Step 28. String the line onto the reel spool (20 minutes)
Step 29. Attach a bobber to the line (2 minutes)
Step 30. Bait the hook with a live worm (2 minutes)
Step 31. Purchase a fish scaling tool (10 minutes)
Step 32. Buy a fishing net (15 minutes)
Step 33. Cast the line into the water (1 minute)
Step 34. Buy a pack of sharp hooks (10 minutes)
Step 35. Secure the hook to the end of the line (5 minutes)
Step 36. Watch a video on how to handle a caught fish (10 minutes)
Step 37. Set the drag on the reel (3 minutes)
Step 38. Learn how to feel for a "nibble" (15 minutes)
Step 39. Attach a leader to the main line (10 minutes)
Step 40. Ask a friend for their favorite fishing spot (5 minutes)
Step 41. Adjust the tension on the reel (5 minutes)
Step 42. Look up the legal size limits for keepable fish (15 minutes)
Step 43. Clean the rod and reel with a damp cloth (10 minutes)
Step 44. Buy a tape measure to check fish length (5 minutes)
Step 45. Find a recipe for pan-fried trout (20 minutes)
Step 46. Check that the rod tip is not cracked (2 minutes)
Step 47. Check the tide or water level charts (10 minutes)
Step 48. Purchase a hat with a brim (15 minutes)
Step 49. Lubricate the reel gears (15 minutes)
Step 50. Borrow a life jacket (10 minutes)
Step 51. Buy a bucket for the catch (10 minutes)
Step 52. Charge your phone for emergency use (2 hours)
Step 53. Test the line strength by pulling it (2 minutes)
Step 54. Pack a lunch for the trip (20 minutes)
Step 55. Buy a pair of waterproof boots (40 minutes)
Step 56. Read about catch-and-release best practices (20 minutes)
Step 57. Wait for a fish to bite (2 hours)
Step 58. Rent a small motorboat (30 minutes)
Step 59. Put on a waterproof jacket (2 minutes)
Step 60. Set up a portable radio (5 minutes)
Step 61. Check the line for any frays or nicks (5 minutes)
Step 62. Browse a sporting goods store (1 hour)
Step 63. Patiently watch the bobber (1 hour)
Step 64. Buy a small scale to weigh the fish (15 minutes)
Step 65. Inquire about boat safety regulations (15 minutes)
Step 66. Sharpen the hooks with a file (10 minutes)
Step 67. Buy a pair of fishing gloves (15 minutes)
Step 68. Select the right weight for the current (10 minutes)
Step 69. Hook the fish firmly (10 seconds)
Step 70. Wind the line onto the reel properly (10 minutes)
